justifications.D1: "the between-family (near vs. decoy) gap will not shrink relative to a prompted-baseline judge" — the format/prior/survivorship failure mode is converted into the F2/F3 detection contrast rather than assumed away.
justifications.D3: "ΔAUC-ROC(FT-paired vs B-prompt) on E-near ... does not exceed 0.03 AUC at the Holm-corrected 0.05 level" — >=2 numeric falsifiers plus a fixed-length no-peeking stopping rule, but none is cheap to evaluate early.
justifications.D4: "confirm the 'will this attempt succeed' signal is present and separable in the archive at all before trusting any FT delta" — leakage, survivorship, prior and population confounds each addressed plus a signal-existence/reachability check.
justifications.D5: "the corpus-first / basins-are-the-ceiling story does not generalize from Ignis's reasoning-trap domain to attempt-record judgment" — names the new cell (attempt-record judgment, paired vs pooled corpora) relative to prior work.
justifications.D6: "the run is declared underpowered rather than the bar lowered post hoc" — F1-F5 pre-commit every branch including pipeline-exercise and no-signal readings.

justifications.D1: "the calibrating kill generalizes past its original confounds and is a property of the archive/objective, not an artifact of the first experiment's hygiene gaps" — the refuted prior is rebuilt into LOSO-primary gates plus a shuffled-label invalidation falsifier.
justifications.D3: "must beat the heuristic floor (arm iii) by >=5pp accuracy/AUC on at least 3 of 4 ... held-out sources" — numeric falsifiers 1-4 plus a frozen-manifest stopping rule, but no cheap early kill before the single training pass.
justifications.D4: "reproducing the 0.228->0.908-style headline check but on hygiene-fixed data, to confirm the fix didn't kill the in-distribution signal outright" — each summary confound has a concrete fix (de-templating, label balance, fitness pass, heuristic floor) plus an in-distribution positive-signal check.
justifications.D5: "H1 confirmed closes the LLM-judge-from-raw-text approach on this archive with a cleaner methodology than the first kill; H0 confirmed reopens it" — a superseding rerun with the confound-removed cell explicitly stated.
justifications.D6: "Any result landing between falsifiers 1 and 3 ... is reported as NOT_ESTABLISHED with both numbers shown side by side" — every branch, including invalidated-leak and NOT-APPLICABLE downgrades, is pre-committed.

justifications.D1: "If truncated-data AUC ≥ 0.68 (within 0.04 of full-data model), reject transfer-learning interpretation; model learned format, not structure" — guards would detect format-dominance, but the design still leads with a naive positive headline and lacks the full decomposition battery (no format-only or prior-only trained controls).
justifications.D3: "Falsifier 1: If fine-tuned AUC < 0.62 on held-out test, hypothesis rejected" — >=2 numeric falsifiers plus a 3-seed stopping rule, with no cheap early independent kill.
justifications.D4: "Force geometric measurement: ablate each input feature (task_id, trace_length, error_count, prior_count) independently" — format, prior, and family-holdout confounds each have a concrete element, but no positive control demonstrating signal detection.
justifications.D5: "Reduced prior skepticism about archive-based transfer" — substantially re-runs the settled fine-tune-a-judge question with a defensible calibration/OOD-family extension.
justifications.D6: "If hold-out family AUC is ≤ 0.56 while in-distribution families hit ≥0.70" — two live hypotheses separate, but mid-band outcomes (e.g., AUC 0.62-0.70 or partial falsifier combinations) have no pre-committed reading.

justifications.D1: "The genuine-judgment residual = raw gain − max(shuffled-label gain, format-only gain, base-rate-only gain)" — the refuted decomposition is rebuilt as the mandatory Phase-3 battery with falsifier 3's CI requirement.
justifications.D3: "if fewer than 3 independent sources each yield ≥100 usable triples ... the experiment HALTS at Phase 0" — a cheap early mechanism-independent falsifier plus Holm-corrected numeric falsifiers 2-5 and a no-threshold-moving stopping rule.
justifications.D4: "positive controls (a known-planted signal) must be run and shown detectable BEFORE a null result is trusted" — every summary confound addressed (format-stripped, base-rate-only, entity- and relation-disjoint splits) plus positive-control and two-sided leakage discipline.
justifications.D5: "relation/domain-disjoint transfer, not just entity-disjoint holdout, is a mandatory split here" — explicitly states the new cell beyond the 2026-06 precedent and the 148-L retraction.
justifications.D6: "reported as an archive-readiness null, not a modeling failure" — all branches, including anti-transfer ("reported exactly as 148-L was, not softened") and pilot-downgrade readings, are pre-committed.

justifications.D1: "Ablation: config-only vs config+outcome" — partial guards exist (permutation null, ablation), but there is no format-only/template decomposition and the success claim is still gated on headline accuracy over a baseline.
justifications.D3: "If any of the 5 preregistered thresholds is violated on the validation set during training, stop immediately" — >=2 numeric falsifiers, an explicit stopping rule, and a cheap early mechanism-independent abort.
justifications.D4: "Re-train on same data with verdict labels shuffled ... Expected: accuracy drops to ~50%" — one relevant confound isolated by design, but the summary's format/template confounds lack concrete elements and there is no positive control.
justifications.D5: "can learn to classify whether a new experiment will receive a pass verdict ... better than domain heuristics" — verdict-prediction from configs is a clearly new question, but there is no statement of the new cell relative to the priors.
justifications.D6: "If (B) achieves >75% accuracy but (A) < 65%, then outcome information is carrying the signal" — two hypotheses receive different predictions, but many outcome combinations (marginal beats, mixed falsifiers) have no pre-committed conclusion.
